subject: Clearpoint onboarding: staging egress, SDK auth & tool-calling next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@clearpoint.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Clearpoint onboarding: staging egress, SDK auth & tool-calling next steps

Alex / team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum for the POC: 

Summary (TL;DR)
- Clearpoint will run a small staging workload against Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) with private egress to your VPC.
- Main items to resolve this week: egress IPs & CIDRs, stub DNS for api.redwood-inference.internal, mTLS for SDK-to-endpoint auth or short-lived tokens, and initial embedding + reranker config for your search use case.

Action items / ask from Clearpoint
1) Provide the CIDR(s) or static IPs you can allocate for egress allowlisting (we need these to provision the NAT / egress rules on our side). If you can’t provide static IPs, confirm whether a VPCE (PrivateLink) endpoint is preferred.
2) Confirm DNS approach: do you want us to expose a private endpoint (VPC endpoint) and you configure split-horizon DNS, or do you prefer we publish IPs and you add an internal A record?
3) Decide auth model for SDK calls: service account mTLS (preferred for long-running service-to-service) vs short-lived OAuth tokens with our runtime-managed rotation. Which is your SRE preference?

What Redwood will provide by EOD Friday
- A minimal architecture diagram for staging with the suggested NAT/egress flow and recommended CIDRs (attached).
- A stub access-request Excel (attached) for your network team to fill in and return (CIDRs, contact, maintenance windows).
- A short SDK integration guide for structured tool-calling (how to format responses as JSON objects that map to your LLM action handlers) and a sample reranker config tuned for embedding-based recall + lightweight lexical features.

Notes on embeddings / reranker (from the call)
- We recommend a 768-d embedding for initial POC (cost/latency balance).
- Reranker: start with our default embedding-similarity score + a small linear model over recency and click-through signals; we can ship a baseline config in the SDK guide.

Next meetings
- Technical deep-dive (SRE + infra): propose Thurs 2027-05-06 10:00 PT. Please confirm availability.

If you prefer, we can do a VPCE-based setup instead of NAT egress — we just need your VPC ID and region.

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: clearpoint-staging-arch-diagram.pdf (2 pages), access-request-template.xlsx (xls, 1 sheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <alex@clearpoint.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clearpoint onboarding: staging egress, SDK auth & tool-calling next steps

Adding a few technical clarifications from the infra side — hi Alex, quick SRE notes: 

1) Egress options
- Preferred: PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint) into our Dedicated control plane. This avoids NAT and simplifies your firewall rules. We'll publish a single endpoint DNS name that resolves privately in your VPC.
- Fallback: NAT egress with fixed Elastic IPs on our side. If you choose this, we will provide a list of 3 static IPs (per region) to allowlist.

2) DNS
- For VPCE approach: you must add a hosted zone delegation (or split-horizon A record) so api.redwood-inference.internal resolves to the VPCE IPs. We can provide the DNS name and the expected private IPs after you share the VPC ID and AZs.

3) mTLS vs token rotation
- mTLS (mutual TLS) requires you to accept our CA and stitch certs into your side; good for persistent service-to-service.
- Short-lived tokens: Redwood issues time-bound JWTs via our token service; this is simpler for browser-based or multi-service integration.
- For the POC, if the traffic is server-to-server, we prefer mTLS for stability; we can support both.

4) Structured output & tool-calling
- The SDK will include helpers to emit structured JSON intents (tool_call objects). We'll add an appendix with the exact schema we recommend so your engineers can plug the handler mappings.

Ben — I attached a minimal proposed firewall matrix (see doc) for the 3-IP fallback. If Alex confirms VPCE, we can skip that.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Chen <alex@clearpoint.ai>

Date: 2027-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clearpoint onboarding: staging egress, SDK auth & tool-calling next steps

Thanks Soojin / Marissa — this looks good. Quick answers from our side: 

1) Egress IPs / VPCE
- We prefer PrivateLink / VPCE if Redwood supports it in us-west-2 — that avoids a lot of our firewall changes. We'll send VPC IDs and the list of AZs by EOD today.

2) DNS
- VPCE is fine; we'll plan to add a split-horizon A record. We'll need the exact DNS name you will publish and the expected private IP ranges so our DNS team can script it.

3) Auth
- For the POC and because the service is server-to-server, our SRE prefers mTLS. We can import Redwood's CA and set up cert rotation with our internal tooling. Please send the certificate authority bundle and instructions.

4) Embeddings / Reranker
- 768-d embeddings sound reasonable; for the reranker we want to try the embedding similarity + click-score weighting first. Can Redwood provide an initial baseline config and a synthetic test set so our ML infra can validate throughput?

5) Logistics
- We'll fill the access-request template and return it.
- Ok to schedule Thurs 2027-05-06 10:00 PT for the deep technical call. Priya (cc) will join from our SRE team.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
VP Product | Clearpoint AI
alex@clearpoint.ai
